**Answer:** The Winter Palace was stormed on the night of 7–8 November 1917 (Gregorian). The main assault and capture came in the early hours of 8 November, which is 26 October in the Julian calendar. The uprising as a whole began on 7 November (25 October Julian). Many sources give 7 November as "the" date because that is the day the revolution began.

I could not fully verify the 8 November capture date. It rests on summarized text, not verbatim quotes, and I did not open a second independent source.

**Verified verbatim (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution, read via fetch):**
- Lead: "It began through an insurrection in Petrograd (now Saint Petersburg) on 7 November 1917 [O.S. 25 October]."
- Infobox: "7 November 1917 [O.S. 25 October]". This is the start of the uprising, not specifically the palace capture.
- Image caption: "The Winter Palace of Petrograd, one day after the insurrection, 8 November".
- Historiography section: "The date 7 November, the anniversary of the October Revolution according to the Gregorian Calendar, was the official national day of the Soviet Union from 1918 onward..."

**Not verified verbatim (summary-extracted only):**
- Lead: "In the early morning of 26 October [N.S. 8 November], they captured the Winter Palace".
- "By 2:10 a.m. on 26 October, Bolshevik forces had gained control."
- The name: "Despite occurring in November of the Gregorian calendar, the event is most commonly known as the October Revolution... because at the time Russia still used the Julian calendar."

**Could not get:** Britannica returned HTTP 403, and the "Assault on the Winter Palace" section text was never read directly. I did not check the page date, and Wikipedia is a secondary source. A primary or scholarly source would be better for the exact hour.

**Answer:** The Winter Palace was stormed on the night of 7–8 November 1917 (Gregorian). The Bolsheviks controlled it by about 2:10 a.m. on 8 November, which is 26 October in the Julian calendar. The revolution as a whole is conventionally dated 7 November (25 October Old Style).

**Confidence:** High for the 7 November (revolution) and 8 November (palace captured) dates. Medium on the exact night split, because sources differ on which night they assign.

**Depth:** Standard. I made one search and two page-reading passes. I did not use the vault, and I wrote nothing to it.

## Findings

- The revolution's start is dated 7 November 1917 (25 October Old Style).
  - Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution
  - Quote: "It began through an insurrection in Petrograd (now Saint Petersburg) on 7 November 1917 [O.S. 25 October]."
- The palace itself was captured in the early hours of 8 November Gregorian (26 October Julian).
  - Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storming_of_the_Winter_Palace. This URL redirects to the October Revolution article.
  - Quote: "In the early morning of 26 October [N.S. 8 November], they captured the Winter Palace"
  - Quote on timing: "By 2:10 a.m. on 26 October, Bolshevik forces had gained control."
  - The page does not label that 2:10 a.m. sentence as Old Style. I inferred it from the article's convention of giving both calendars.
- The Julian-to-Gregorian offset in 1917 was 13 days. 25 October Old Style plus 13 days is 7 November, and 26 October is 8 November.
  - I did not cite a separate source for the offset. It is arithmetic, and both Wikipedia date pairs agree with it.

## Conflicts and gaps

- **One source gives a different night.**
  - Source: https://historycollection.com/russian-revolution-dates-february-october-1917/
  - It says "On the night of October 24-25 by the Julian calendar — November 7, 1917 by the Gregorian calendar — Bolshevik Red Guards..."
  - That is a tertiary source and differs from Wikipedia. I trust the Wikipedia dating more because it gives a specific 2:10 a.m. time for the palace.
- **"7 November" can mean two things.** It is the date of the insurrection's start, and many sources use it loosely for the storming. The palace fell after midnight, on 8 November.
- **I could not read Britannica.** The page returned 403, so I did not use it.
- **Wikipedia is the only source for the palace-capture date.** I did not find an independent second source for that detail.
- **I could not check the last ~74,000 characters of the Wikipedia article.**
